rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ويعقوب برواية روح وزيد
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu ʿAmr, and Yaʿqub through Rawḥ and Zayd read mustaqarr with kasra on the qāf; the remaining readers use fatḥa.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ويعقوب برواية روح وزيد فمستقر بكسر القاف

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The remaining readers pronounce the qāf of mustaqarr with fatḥa.
rows.anchor: والباقون بفتح القاف

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: With kasra, mustaqirr means a settled person, so the implied predicate is minkum: some of you are settled in wombs.
rows.anchor: من كسر القاف كان المستقر بمعنى القار

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: With fatḥa, istiqrār is intransitive, so mustaqarr names a place, with lakum as its implied predicate.
rows.anchor: من فتح فليس على أنه مفعول ألا ترى أن أستقر لا يتعدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istawdaʿ is transitive to two objects; mustawdaʿ can mean the person deposited there or the place receiving the deposit.
rows.anchor: استودعت زيدا ألفا وأودعت زيدا ألفا فاستودع مثل أودع

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: On the fatḥa reading, both nouns can denote places: a place of settling and a place of deposit.
rows.anchor: جعل المستودع مكانا ليكون مثل المعطوف عليه أي فلكم مكان استقرار واستيداع

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: On the kasra reading, some are settled in wombs and some deposited in loins; mustawdaʿ is a passive patient, not a place.
rows.anchor: من قرأ فمستقر فالمعنى منكم مستقر في الأرحام ومنكم مستودع في الأصلاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created stars for human benefit and guidance in travel, navigation, finding the qibla, reckoning night hours, and following land and sea routes by their light, rising, and positions.
rows.anchor: لأن من النجوم ما يكون بين يدي الإنسان ومنها ما يكون خلفه ومنها ما يكون عن يمينه

rows.speaker: البلخي
rows.claim: The guidance purpose does not exclude other great purposes; varied star sizes, courses, and relations, and the sun and moon's benefits to life, show this.
rows.anchor: وقال البلخي: ليس في قوله:

rows.speaker: علي بن إبراهيم بن هاشم
rows.claim: In the Tafsīr of ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, the stars signify the family of Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير علي بن إبراهيم بن هاشم أن النجوم آل محمد ع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs have been made clear as proofs and evidences for people who reflect and thereby know.
rows.anchor: أي بينا الحجج والبينات: { لقوم يعلمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All people descend from Adam, and Eve was created from one of his ribs; their shared origin encourages affection, compassion, and fellowship.
rows.anchor: لأن الناس إذا رجعوا إلى أصل واحد كانوا أقرب إلى التواد والتعاطف والتآلف

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says a person is settled in the womb until birth and deposited in the grave until resurrection.
rows.anchor: مستقر في الرحم إلى أن يولد ومستودع في القبر إلى أن يبعث عن عبد الله بن مسعود

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وعكرمة عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and ʿIkrima report from Ibn ʿAbbās that the wombs are the place of settlement and the fathers' loins the place of deposit.
rows.anchor: مستقر في بطون الأمهات ومستودع في أصلاب الآباء عن سعيد بن جبير وعكرمة عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid places settlement on earth in this life and deposit with God in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: مستقر على ظهر الأرض في الدنيا ومستودع عند الله في الآخرة عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says a person's settlement is the span of life, while the place of deposit is where one dies and is raised.
rows.anchor: مستقرها أيام حياتها ومستودعها حيث يموت وحيث يبعث عن أبي العالية

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the world is a person's place of deposit and the grave the place of settlement; he likens people to a trust returned to its owner, citing Labīd and Sulaymān ibn Zayd.
rows.anchor: مستقر في القبر ومستودع في الدنيا عن الحسن وكان يقول يا ابن آدم أنت وديعة في أهلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated declaration urges reflection and signals that each item mentioned is a sign of God's oneness and exalted attributes; the knowledgeable and discerning are singled out as its beneficiaries.
rows.anchor: وكرر قوله قد فصلنا الآيات حثا على النظر وتنبيها على أن كلا مما ذكر آية ودلالة تدل على توحيده

rows.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم برواية أبي يوسف الأعشى والبرجمي وعلي بن أبي طالب وعبد الله بن مسعود والأعمش ويحيى بن يعمر
rows.claim: These readers use the nominative jannāt, coordinating it grammatically with qinwān by form even though the items differ in kind.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو بكر عن عاصم برواية أبي يوسف الأعشى والبرجمي وجنات بالرفع وهو قراءة أمير المؤمنين علي بن أبي طالب

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The remaining readers use the accusative jannāt, coordinating it with khidran.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون وجنات على النصب

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف
rows.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Khalaf read thumuri with two ḍammas, including the occurrences in the commands to eat and in Yā Sīn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف ثمره بضمتين وكذلك كلوا من ثمره وفي سورة ياسين ليأكلوا من ثمره

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The remaining readers pronounce thamar with two fatḥas in all the cited occurrences.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون ثمره بفتحتين في الجميع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With accusative jannāt, the word coordinates with khidran: God brings forth green growth and grape gardens from the water.
rows.anchor: من قرأ وجنات فإنه عطفها على قوله خضرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominative jannāt coordinates with qinwān by grammatical form despite their different categories, as in the poet's pairing of a sword and spear.
rows.anchor: فإنه عطفها على قنوان لفظا وإن لم يكن من جنسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamar can be the singular collective, just as baqara/bāqir and shajara/shajar pair singular and collective forms.
rows.anchor: فالثمر جمع ثمرة مثل بقرة وبقر وشجرة وشجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two-ḍamma reading can derive thumur from singular thamara like khashaba/khashab and akama/akam, as the poet's line illustrates.
rows.anchor: مثل خشبة وخشب وأكمة وأكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, thumur is a collective plural of thimār, a plural of thamarah; qāra/qūr and nāqah/sāḥah/sūḥ offer analogous patterns.
rows.anchor: والآخر أن يكون جمع ثمار على ثمر فيكون ثمر جمع الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khiḍr means green or fresh; Arabs also use akhḍar for black, call Iraq's lush land Sawād, and describe fertile, spacious people or places as green. A cited poem calls the poet green-skinned and a notable Arab.
rows.anchor: وقال الفضل بن عباس بن عتبة بن أبي لهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hadith calls worldly life sweet and green, meaning tender and flourishing; the expressions 'his blood went green' and 'took it green' mean vainly and for free.
rows.anchor: أي غضة ناعمة وذهب دمه خضرا أي باطلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mutarākib means piled or layered, from the form of rukūb.
rows.anchor: ومتراكب متفاعل من الركوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭalʿ is the first emergence of the palm's fruit; qinwān is plural of qinw, a bunch or cluster, and dāniya means close at hand.
rows.anchor: والقنوان جمع قنو وهو العذق بكسر العين أي الكباسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yanaʿ and yanʿ mean ripening; the poet's olives have ripened. Yanʿ may also be a plural like ṣāḥib/ṣaḥb and tājir/tajar.
rows.anchor: والينع والنضج يقال ينع الثمر ينعا وينعا وأينع إذا أدرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here sky means cloud; in Arabic anything above that casts shade can be called samāʾ.
rows.anchor: يريد من السحاب والعرب تقول كل ما علاك فأطلك فهو سماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water grows the food of livestock, birds, wild animals, and humans, sustaining their nourishment and growth; this is preferable to taking the phrase as all botanical kinds.
rows.anchor: والأول أحسن وإنما قال به لأنه سبحانه جعله سببا مؤديا إلى النبات لا مولدا له

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ allows that the phrase means all varieties of plants, taking kull shayʾ as botanical species, as in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: المراد أخرجنا به من جميع أنواع النبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Water is a means leading to growth, not an independently generative cause: God could have brought forth plants without it.
rows.anchor: جعله سببا مؤديا إلى النبات لا مولدا له وقد كان يمكنه الإنبات بغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The green growth is a fresh green crop, the stalk of the grain ear; 'from it' is understood as from the water.
rows.anchor: فأخرجنا منه } أي من الماء. وقيل: من النبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grain comes from the green crop, with its kernels layered one over another, as in wheat and sesame ears.
rows.anchor: أي من ذلك الزرع الخضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God also brings forth bunches of ripe dates from the palms' flower clusters; the bunches are within reach.
rows.anchor: أي ونخرج من النخل

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: The verse mentions nearby bunches and leaves distant ones implicit: as garments shielding from heat also shield from cold, the context supplies what is omitted.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل ومنها قنوان بعيدة لأن في الكلام دليلا على البعيدة السحيقة

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: Another explanation is that abundant, heavy fruit pulls the bunches close to the ground.
rows.anchor: دانية دنت من الأرض لكثرة ثمرها وثقل حملها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The flower cluster is singled out because it bears fine, nourishing food unavailable in the fruit's outer casings.
rows.anchor: وإنما خص الطلع بالذكر لما فيه من المنافع والأغذية الشريفة التي ليست في أكمام الثمار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water also brings forth grape orchards; in the nominative reading, the implied verb is 'We bring forth.'
rows.anchor: يعني وأخرجنا به أيضا جنات من أعناب أي بساتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Olive and pomegranate refer to their trees; their leaves cover the branch from one end to the other, as the poet's ripened pomegranate and olives illustrate.
rows.anchor: ومعناه أن ورقهما يشتمل على العود كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trees resemble one another while differing in taste.
rows.anchor: أي مشتبها شجره يشبه بعضه بعضا وغير متشابه في الطعم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says the leaves resemble one another while the fruits differ.
rows.anchor: مشتبها ورقه مختلفا ثمره عن قتادة

rows.speaker: قول غير مسمى
rows.claim: Another reported view says the plants resemble one another in form but differ in taste.
rows.anchor: وقيل: مشتبها في الخلق مختلفا في الطعم

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says things of one kind resemble one another, while things of different kinds do not.
rows.anchor: مشتبها ما كان من جنس واحد وغير متشابه إذا اختلف جنسه عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best reading includes all the reported likenesses and differences: fruits resemble in some respects and differ in others.
rows.anchor: والأولى أن يقال أن جميع ذلك مشتبه من وجوه مختلف من وجوه فيدخل فيه جميع ما تقدم

words: ٱنظُرُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰ ثَمَرِهِۦٓ إِذَآ أَثْمَرَ وَيَنْعِهِۦٓ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Observe fruit from its first appearance to ripeness and how taste, color, smell, and size change; this reveals a maker who governs it.
rows.anchor: من ابتداء خروجه إذا أثمر إلى انتهائه إذا أينع وأدرك كيف تنتقل عليه الأحوال في الطعم واللون والرائحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The well-formed crops and diverse fruits point to a creator who knowingly distinguished them before bringing them into being and governs their growth; believers benefit by drawing this inference.
rows.anchor: لدلالات على أن لها خالقا قصد إلى التمييز بينها قبل خلقها على علم بها

rows.speaker: أهل المدينة ويعقوب
rows.claim: The Medinan readers and Yaʿqūb read maytan with a doubled yāʾ.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة ويعقوب ميتا بالتشديد

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The remaining readers use the light pronunciation, without doubling.
rows.anchor: والباقون بالتخفيف

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda treats the light form as a shortened form with the same meaning; Abū al-Raʿlā al-Ghassānī's poem calls the despairing living truly dead.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: الميتة تخفيف ميتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second of the two yāʾs is deleted; it had changed from wāw and underwent deletion like a letter altered by substitution.
rows.anchor: والمحذوف من الياءين الثانية المنقلبة عن الواو وأعلت بالحذف كما أعلت بالقلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akābir is a plural of akbar; Arabic also has akābira and aṣāghira, illustrated by a poet's use of aḥāmira.
rows.anchor: الأكابر جمع الأكبر وقد قالوا الأكابرة والأصاغرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root of makr is twisting; makr figuratively twists a person away from sound guidance.
rows.anchor: وأصل المكر الفتل ومنه جارية ممكورة أي مفتلة البدن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative hamza attaches to the conjunction wāw as a rhetorical question seeking acknowledgment.
rows.anchor: أومن هذه همزة الاستفهام دخلت على واو العطف وهو استفهام يراد به التقرير

words: كَذَٰلِكَ جَعَلْنَا فِى كُلِّ قَرْيَةٍ أَكَٰبِرَ مُجْرِمِيهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kāf in 'likewise We made' is accusative, coordinated with the preceding clause; mujrimīhā can be fronted in sense or governed by the iḍāfa to akābir.
rows.anchor: موضع الكاف في قوله: { وكذلك جعلنا } نصب معطوفة على ما قبلها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the verse came down concerning Ḥamza and Abū Jahl: after Abū Jahl harmed the Prophet, Ḥamza struck him with a bow and embraced Islam.
rows.anchor: نزلت في حمزة بن عبد المطلب وأبي جهل بن هاشم

rows.speaker: عكرمة وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: Another report, from ʿIkrima and transmitted from Abū Jaʿfar, places the occasion in ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir's conversion, contrasted with Abū Jahl.
rows.anchor: في عمار بن ياسر حين آمن وأبي جهل عن عكرمة وهو المروي عن أبي جعفر

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the verse was revealed concerning ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.
rows.anchor: نزلت في عمر بن الخطاب عن الضحاك

rows.speaker: الحسن وجماعة
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and a group take the verse as a general comparison of every believer and unbeliever; the author prefers this broader reading, which encompasses the specific reports.
rows.anchor: عامة في كل مؤمن وكافر عن الحسن وجماعة وهذا أولى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, and Mujāhid explain the dead person as an unbeliever whom God revives by guiding to faith, likening unbelief to death and faith to life.
rows.anchor: أي كافرا فاحييناه بأن هديناه إلى الإيمان عن ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد

rows.speaker: قول غير مسمى
rows.claim: Another view takes the dead person as a sperm drop brought to life, as in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه من كان نطفة فأحييناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is knowledge and wisdom, called light because they guide to right conduct as physical light guides on roads.
rows.anchor: أحدها: أن المراد بالنور العلم والحكمة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid identifies the light as the Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: وثانيها: إن المراد بالنور هنا القرآن عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the light as faith.
rows.anchor: وثالثها: أن المراد به الإيمان عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A disbeliever is called dead because neither he nor others benefit from his life; unlike the dead, he also incurs punishment and harms others. A believer is alive because his life benefits himself and others.
rows.anchor: وإنما سمى الله تعالى الكافر ميتا لأنه لا ينتفع بحياته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurʾān, faith, and knowledge are called light because they guide people from unbelief and confused error as other lights guide the way; unbelief is darkness because it does not guide or disclose right conduct.
rows.anchor: وسمى القرآن والإيمان والعلم نورا لأن الناس يبصرون بذلك ويهتدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbeliever's blindness parallels the images in the verses about one who is blind and the contrast between blind and seeing.
rows.anchor: وهذا كما سمى الكافر أعمى في قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording is elliptical: 'like one whose likeness is in darkness' means 'like one who is in darkness'; the expression is framed through the person's likeness.
rows.anchor: لم يقل سبحانه كمن هو في الظلمات تقديره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison is that unbelief was adorned for these people and they practiced it, as faith was adorned for the earlier people and they practiced it; each group's condition is compared in its adornment.
rows.anchor: معناه زين لهؤلاء الكفر فعملوه مثل ما زين لأولئك الإيمان فعملوه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says Satan and their own selves adorned their deeds, citing the report that devils inspire their allies.
rows.anchor: روي عن الحسن أنه قال زينه والله لهم الشيطان وأنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive 'was adorned' does not require an adornment agent distinct from the people, as in the idioms 'he admired himself' and 'he was devoted to this.'
rows.anchor: وقوله: { زين } لا يقتضي مزينا غيرهم

words: كَذَٰلِكَ جَعَلْنَا فِى كُلِّ قَرْيَةٍ أَكَٰبِرَ مُجْرِمِيهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As with the preceding adornment, God made the chief criminals in each town prominent and enabled the plotting criminal just as he made the believer's light; the former stray by bad choice, while the latter are guided by good choice. For believers this making is grace; for criminals it is empowerment to plot. Chiefs are singled out because their power over all makes God's power over the lesser evident all the more.
rows.anchor: فكل ما فعلنا بهؤلاء فعلنا بأولئك إلا أن أولئك اهتدوا بحسن اختيارهم وهؤلاء ضلوا بسوء اختيارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in 'so that they plot' marks an outcome, also called the lām of becoming, as in the account of Moses being adopted to become an enemy and in the poet's verse.
rows.anchor: واللام في قوله: { ليمكروا فيها } لام العاقبة ويسمى لام الصيرورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their plotting harms themselves when its punishment comes; a person cannot literally conceal his scheme from himself, though he can conceal it from others.
rows.anchor: لأن عقاب ذلك يحل بهم ولا يصح أن يمكر الإنسان بنفسه على الحقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The point is that the chief criminals did not plot against believers as rivals to God: their being enabled to plot underscores that they do not contend with Him.
rows.anchor: لم يمكروا بالمؤمنين على وجه المغالبة لله إذ هم كأنه سبحانه جعلهم ليمكروا

rows.speaker: حفص وروح
rows.claim: Ḥafṣ and Rawḥ read 'the day He gathers them' with yāʾ; the remaining readers use nūn, with the cited verse supporting the nūn form.
rows.anchor: قرأ حفص وروح ويوم يحشرهم بالياء والباقون بالنون

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj parses khālidīn as an accusative circumstantial; the fire is their abode while they remain eternally there.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: خالدين فيها منصوب على الحال

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī takes mathwā as a verbal noun, not a place noun, because the construction has a governed circumstantial; the sense is that the fire is your enduring stay, with the pronoun as semantic subject.
rows.anchor: المثوى عندي في الآية اسم للمصدر دون المكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse turns from what precedes to the gathering of all creatures. Other views restrict the gathering to humans and jinn because their exchange follows, or to unbelievers; the day is governed by an implicit 'He says.'
rows.anchor: وقيل: الإنس والجن لأنه يتعقبه حديثهم

words: يَٰمَعْشَرَ ٱلْجِنِّ قَدِ ٱسْتَكْثَرْتُم مِّنَ ٱلْإِنسِ
rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains the jinn as having greatly multiplied those humans whom they led astray; Ibn ʿAbbās glosses this as misleading and luring humans.
rows.anchor: قد استكثرتم ممن أضللتموه من الإنس عن الزجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation: humans took jinn as leaders and followed their desires, while humans enjoyed the pleasures and sensual appetites the jinn adorned for them.
rows.anchor: أن اتخذهم الإنس قادة ورؤساء فاتبعوا أهواءهم

rows.speaker: الحسن وابن جريج والزجاج
rows.claim: Another explanation concerns humans seeking refuge from jinn: travelers called on the lord of a valley, believing the jinn would protect them; the jinn in turn took pleasure and benefit in being believed able to help or harm.
rows.anchor: واستمتاع الجن بالإنس أن الجن إذا اعتقدوا أن الإنس يتعوذون بهم

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb says the mutual enjoyment means that each side obeyed and agreed with the other.
rows.anchor: أن المراد بالاستمتاع طاعة بعضهم لبعض وموافقة بعضهم بعضا عن محمد بن كعب

rows.speaker: البلخي
rows.claim: Al-Balkhī allows that enjoyment is restricted to humans: people enjoyed one another, without the jinn included as participants.
rows.anchor: قال البلخي: ويحتمل أن يكون الاستمتاع مقصورا عن الإنس

rows.speaker: الحسن والسدي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Suddī take the appointed term as death.
rows.anchor: يعني بالأجل الموت عن الحسن والسدي

rows.speaker: قول غير مسمى
rows.claim: Another view takes the appointed term as resurrection and gathering: resurrection is the term for requital, just as death is the term for making up what passed.
rows.anchor: وقيل: البعث والحشر لأن الحشر أجل الجزاء

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī argues that the verse implies one lifespan: if there were two terms, someone killed before dying naturally would not have reached his term, yet they say they reached it.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا دلالة على أنه لا أجل إلا واحد لأنه لو كان أجلان

rows.speaker: علي بن عيسى وغيره من البغداديين
rows.claim: ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā and other Baghdādī theologians reject that inference: the verse does not rule out separate terms for death and resurrection, or for death and a possible full lifespan.
rows.anchor: من البغداديين لا دلالة في الآية على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God says the fire is their abode: they will remain there forever under punishment, subject to the stated exception.
rows.anchor: أي دائمين مؤبدين فيها معذبين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the threat against unbelievers was initially open-ended, then made definite by the verse declaring that God does not forgive associating partners.
rows.anchor: ما روي عن ابن عباس أنه قال كان وعيد الكفار مبهما غير مقطوع به

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj takes the exception to cover the interval from resurrection through gathering and judgment, or the additional punishment God wills.
rows.anchor: وثانيها: أن الاستثناء إنما هو من القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view makes the exception about sinful Muslims, whom God may punish justly according to their deserts or forgive by grace.
rows.anchor: الاستثناء راجع إلى غير الكفار من عصاة المسلمين الذين هم في مشيئة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ takes the exception to mean those among them who believed.
rows.anchor: ورابعها: أن معناه إلا ما شاء الله ممن آمن منهم عن عطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is wise in his acts and knows everything; another explanation emphasizes that he knows who merits punishment or reward and the measure each merits, and chooses whom to punish or forgive.
rows.anchor: أي محكم لأفعاله عليم بكل شيء

rows.speaker: علي بن عيسى
rows.claim: ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā compares this entrusting of tyrants to one another with God's allowing them to dominate during a trial, so deserved requital can follow their actions.
rows.anchor: كذلك المهل بتخلية بعضهم عن بعض للامتحان الذي معه يصح الجزاء على الأعمال

rows.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Jubbāʾī says that on Judgment Day God leaves tyrants to one another, sending followers back to leaders to ask them to free them from punishment; this shows no ally can avert it.
rows.anchor: ونقول للأتباع قولوا للمتبوعين حتى يخلصوكم من العذاب عن أبي علي الجبائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation links the phrase to the preceding dispute: just as God gathered jinn and humans into the fire and made them responsible for one another, he treats other wrongdoers similarly in requital.
rows.anchor: لما حكى الله تعالى ما يجري بين الجن والإنس من الخصام والجدال في الآخرة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God puts the best people over those with whom he is pleased and the worst over those with whom he is angry, in recompense for their sins.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس: إذا رضي الله عن قوم ولى أمرهم خيارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The retribution follows people's own deeds, as in the declaration that God does not change a people until they change what is within themselves.
rows.anchor: إن الله لا يغير ما بقوم حتى يغيروا ما بأنفسهم

rows.speaker: الكلبي عن مالك بن دينار
rows.claim: A wisdom-book report says God owns rulers' hearts: he makes them mercy for people who obey him and affliction for those who disobey, and urges repentance instead of cursing rulers.
rows.anchor: الكلبي عن مالك بن دينار قال: قرأت في بعض كتب الحكمة

rows.speaker: قول غير مسمى
rows.claim: One view glosses the phrase as leaving wrongdoers to one another and to what they choose, without supporting them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معنى قوله نولي بعضهم بعضا نخلي بينهم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda takes the phrase to mean that wrongdoers follow one another into the fire, using walāya in the sense of succession.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه نتابع بعضهم بعضا في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ẓufr means a nail or claw; a person with long nails is called aẓfar, by analogy with aʿshar for someone with long hair.
rows.anchor: الظفر ظفر الإنسان وغيره ورجل أظفر إذا كان طويل الأظفار

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj gives the singulars of ḥawāyā as ḥāwiya, ḥāwiyāʾ, and ḥawiyya, for what gathers and coils inside the belly.
rows.anchor: واحدها حاوية وحاوياء وحوية وهي ما يحوى في البطن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥawāyā can be nominative, coordinated with ẓuhūrihimā, or accusative, coordinated with the object after illā; mā ikhtalaṭa is likewise coordinated with that object.
rows.anchor: موضع الحوايا يحتمل أن يكون رفعا عطفا على الظهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhālika is best parsed in the accusative as the second object of jazaynāhum; parsing it as a subject would produce a construction only allowed in poetic necessity.
rows.anchor: مفعول ثان لجزيناهم التقدير جزيناهم ذلك ببغيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restrictions described were imposed on the Jews in Moses' time.
rows.anchor: على اليهود في أيام موسى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير وقتادة ومجاهد والسدي
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Qatāda, Mujāhid, and al-Suddī include animals without split toes, such as camels, ostriches, geese, and ducks.
rows.anchor: كل ما ليس بمنفرج الأصابع كالإبل والنعام والأوز والبط عن ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير وقتادة ومجاهد والسدي

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd restricts the phrase to camels.
rows.anchor: هو الإبل فقط عن ابن زيد

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī includes predators, dogs, cats, and animals that hunt with claws.
rows.anchor: يدخل فيه كل السباع والكلاب والسنانير وما يصطاد بظفره عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: القُتيبي والبلخي
rows.claim: Al-Qutaybī and al-Balkhī include every clawed bird and every hoofed animal.
rows.anchor: كل ذي مخلب من الطير وكل ذي حافر من الدواب عن القتيبي والبلخي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God forbade Jews the fat of cattle and sheep, including the caul, kidney fat, and other fat inside them.
rows.anchor: أنه كان حرم عليهم شحوم البقر والغنم من الثرب وشحم الكلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fat borne on the backs was excepted; the text describes it as the fatty flesh, which was not forbidden.
rows.anchor: من الشحم وهو اللحم السمين فإنه لم يحرم عليهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وسعيد بن جبير وقتادة ومجاهد والسدي
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Qatāda, Mujāhid, and al-Suddī identify al-ḥawāyā as the intestines or abdominal organs; their fat was likewise excepted.
rows.anchor: والحوايا هي المباعر عن ابن عباس والحسن وسعيد بن جبير وقتادة ومجاهد والسدي

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets al-ḥawāyā as the milk-producing glands.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هي بنات اللبن عن ابن زيد

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī takes al-ḥawāyā as the intestines on which fat lies.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هي الأمعاء التي عليها الشحوم عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: ابن جريج والسدي
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj and al-Suddī say the exception includes the flank fat and the rump fat attached to the coccyx.
rows.anchor: وهو شحم الجنب والألية لأنه على العصعص عن ابن جريج والسدي

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says the rump was not included, because it was not named in the exception and the coccyx does not count as bone here.
rows.anchor: الألية لم تدخل في هذا لأنها لم تستثن عن الجبائي
